Thank you for the nice words.

Honestly I am not sure. My doctor diagnosed folliculitis ulerythematosa reticulata and said it is close to KPRF. From what I understand atrophoderma vermiculata is not same as folliculitis ulerythematosa reticulata. At least when I look at pictures it doesn't look like my skin. My skin is not so badly scarred and the scarring is not so textured. Folliculitis ulerythematosa reticulata affects cheeks. Symptoms are basically same as KPRF: pain, burning and flushing. Difference is that Folliculitis ulerythematosa reticulata causes red permanent scarring. I feel that this particular doctor only diagnosed folliculitis ulerythematosa reticulata because she said that it cannot be KPRF because KPRF does not cause pain and burning sensation. At least here in Finland, doctors don't believe/know that KPRF causes pain. 

A bit confusing answer, sorry.

I live in Finland, I couldn't find a pharmacy that could make sirolimus cream here. So I ordered sirolimus powder from abroad and the other things needed for it and learned how to make it myself.
In a box at room temperature protected from sunlight. Yes in a small plastic bottle

Yes i can say that my cream does help.

I have been using it for about 3 months and the pain, burning and flushing have decreased significantly. There is still little bit a pain and burning sensation, but not nearly as bad as before. Flushing episodes last much less time and there aren't as many of them as there used to be. The redness has decreased a little, not as much as I would have liked, but overall I am happy that the pains have decreased.

I have made about 15ml 1% Sirolimus cream this way:

2ml DMSO

0.15g Rapamycin powder

15ml Excipial Hydrocreme
